- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.7) and model forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If recent true outcomes show sharp downward spikes after high peaks, model should adjust downward with lagged momentum correction.  
- When official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, forecast should not rise above 10% above recent 7-day average.  
- If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days falling), reduce forecast slope by 15-20% for next 5 days.  
- For events with high bearish sentiment (≥0.3) and negative supply net, model should not forecast > 5% above 14-day moving average.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model should avoid linear extrapolation and use weighted average of recent 3-5 day highs/lows.  
- When official events include CAP3 EU or DE auctions, forecast should be capped at 10% below recent 14-day high if sentiment is neutral or bearish.  
- If model forecast is rising faster than 1.5% per day and true outcome shows downward correction, apply “sudden deceleration” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for next 3 days.
